Let \(r_{ij}=1/c_{ij}\) be the resistance of edge \(\{i,j\}\), and let
\[
W=\sum_i\sum_{j\sim i}c_{ij}=2\sum_{e}c_e.
\]
For a weighted tree,
\[
C_{ij}=W\sum_{e\in[i,j]}r_e.
\]
Thus commute times are a positive scalar multiple of tree-path resistance distances.

Since
\[
C_{13}=C_{12}+C_{23},\qquad C_{24}=C_{23}+C_{34},
\]
the tree must be the path
\[
1-2-3-4.
\]
Moreover, for its three edges,
\[
Wr_{12}=4,\qquad Wr_{23}=6,\qquad Wr_{34}=12.
\]
Hence
\[
c_{12}:c_{23}:c_{34}
=\frac14:\frac16:\frac1{12}
=3:2:1.
\]
Therefore the transition probabilities are
\[
P(2,1)=\frac35,\quad P(2,3)=\frac25,
\]
\[
P(3,2)=\frac23,\quad P(3,4)=\frac13,
\]
with \(1\to2\) and \(4\to3\) deterministically.

Set \(T\) equal to the first time the walk reaches either endpoint \(1\) or \(4\).

### 1. First endpoint reached

Let \(q_i=P_i(T_1<T_4)\). Then
\[
q_2=\frac35+\frac25q_3,\qquad q_3=\frac23q_2,
\]
so
\[
q_2=\frac9{11},\qquad P_2(T_4<T_1)=\frac2{11}.
\]

The first moment of \(T\) satisfies
\[
m_2=1+\frac25m_3,\qquad m_3=1+\frac23m_2,
\]
giving
\[
E_2T=m_2=\frac{21}{11}.
\]

The second moment satisfies
\[
s_2=1+\frac25(2m_3+s_3),\qquad
s_3=1+\frac23(2m_2+s_2),
\]
so
\[
E_2T^2=s_2=\frac{699}{121}.
\]

We also need the mixed first and second moments on the event \(A=\{T_1<T_4\}\). Solving the corresponding recurrences gives
\[
E_2[T\,1_A]=\frac{171}{121},\qquad
E_2[T^2\,1_A]=\frac{5409}{1331}.
\]
Therefore
\[
E_2[T\,1_{A^c}]
=\frac{21}{11}-\frac{171}{121}
=\frac{60}{121},
\]
and
\[
E_2[T^2\,1_{A^c}]
=\frac{699}{121}-\frac{5409}{1331}
=\frac{2280}{1331}.
\]

### 2. Time to reach the other endpoint

If the first endpoint is \(1\), let \(S_1\) be the time from \(1\) to \(4\). Solving the hitting-time recurrences gives
\[
E_1S_1=16,\qquad E_1S_1^2=451.
\]

If the first endpoint is \(4\), let \(S_4\) be the time from \(4\) to \(1\). Then
\[
E_4S_4=6,\qquad E_4S_4^2=61.
\]

By the strong Markov property,
\[
\tau_{\rm cov}=T+
\begin{cases}
S_1,&A,\\
S_4,&A^c.
\end{cases}
\]

Thus
\[
E_2\tau_{\rm cov}
=\frac{21}{11}+\frac9{11}(16)+\frac2{11}(6)
=\frac{177}{11}.
\]

For the second moment,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_2\tau_{\rm cov}^2
&=E_2T^2
+2\left(16E_2[T1_A]+6E_2[T1_{A^c}]\right)\\
&\quad+\frac9{11}(451)+\frac2{11}(61)\\
&=\frac{52882}{121}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Var}_2(\tau_{\rm cov})
=\frac{52882}{121}-\left(\frac{177}{11}\right)^2
=\frac{21553}{121}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(C_{14},\mathbb E_2\tau_{\rm cov},\operatorname{Var}_2(\tau_{\rm cov})\right)
=
\left(22,\frac{177}{11},\frac{21553}{121}\right)}
\]
